headline: Pricing, forecasting, and sales tools the Energy team trusts, run from one set of commercial data.
pitch: I run sales operations from the data up, and I also run a sales team. At flyExclusive I report to the Chief Commercial Officer and own the CRM (HubSpot Enterprise), the performance dashboards leadership reviews, and the sales tools reps use every day. I built the Python competitive-pricing app behind our 2026 pricing tables, run the decision analytics on contract concessions, and built AI proposal and agreement tools that save reps 1 to 2 hours per lead. At the start of H2 2026 I re-forecast sales for the rest of the year, and actuals have tracked much closer to my numbers than to the original plan. Since May 2026 I've also been interim manager of the retail sales team, about 20 reps doing roughly $10M in sales a month. I'm based in Raleigh, close to the Fuquay-Varina site, and the travel works for me.

requirements.need: Lead pricing governance and pricing analytics to find margin opportunities and leakage
requirements.evidence: I built and shipped a Python competitive-pricing web app for flyExclusive's retail sales team that analyzes competitor and market pricing; it directly informed the 2026 pricing tables and strategy. I also run the decision analytics on sales concessions in contracts, which is where margin leaks. My AI proposal and agreement tools mean reps can only send company-approved terms.

requirements.need: Own sales forecasting and pipeline management with Sales Leadership
requirements.evidence: At the start of H2 2026 I revised flyExclusive's financial plan with new sales projections for the rest of the year, and actuals have tracked much closer to my revision than to the original plan. At TRANZACT I built forecasting models with commercial and finance leadership. As interim sales manager I review the pipeline with the team myself.

requirements.need: Sales enablement tools, training, and CRM effectiveness
requirements.evidence: I led flyExclusive's HubSpot Enterprise transformation (cut ~300 contact properties to ~100 governed ones, deduplication, Master Data Management, lead routing by product expertise with a round robin for the rest) and onboarded 10 sales reps and 5 marketers onto it. I run biweekly office hours for the sales team: a planned lesson, then open questions. My LLM pipeline enriched ~500,000 CRM records, and personalized outreach got a 150% better response rate.

requirements.need: Manage commercial data, customer segmentation, and sales structure
requirements.evidence: I designed the CRM data architecture and MDM that give flyExclusive's sales organization one source of truth, and built attribution frameworks that identify high-value customer segments. At TRANZACT I ran segmentation and a structured A/B testing program (50% win rate, 30% CTR improvement).

requirements.need: Support sales targets, KPIs, and performance metrics
requirements.evidence: As interim manager of a ~20-person retail sales team doing ~$10M a month, I work to targets and track rep performance on the dashboards I built. At TRANZACT I partnered with commercial and finance leadership on sales performance analytics that guided investment and field-activity planning.

requirements.need: Deliver insights on sales performance, pipeline health, customer trends, and scenario analysis
requirements.evidence: I turn commercial data into recommendations leadership acts on: attribution and forecasting at TRANZACT, funnel dashboards and conversational reporting (ask-a-question access to the data) at flyExclusive. My attribution case study includes an interactive model that shows how each scenario changes the plan.

requirements.need: Collaboration, decision-making, and influence without direct authority
requirements.evidence: flyExclusive's sending domain was rated "Bad" in Google Postmaster, so marketing email was going to spam, while sales leadership wanted to mail the biggest list possible. I made the case for trimming to engaged, opted-in contacts, and open rates doubled. I write a PRD and get sign-off before every build, and present build priorities to the Chief Commercial Officer monthly.

requirements.need: Oversee quoting, order management, backlog visibility, and customer service processes
requirements.evidence: I rebuilt flyExclusive's website with pipelines that feed quote requests straight into the CRM, the proposal tools standardize what goes out, and I'm now building a billing integration into the CRM and our mobile app. I haven't run order management or backlog for manufactured products; I'd learn TE's order-to-delivery flow with Supply Chain and Customer Service first.

requirements.need: Lead end-to-end tender processes and track tender win rates and profitability
requirements.evidence: Formal utility tenders are new to me. The pieces I'd bring are bid content built from approved templates (my proposal tools), pricing analysis, and win-rate tracking from the CRM. I'd start by mapping the current tender calendar and building a win/loss and margin view by tender.

requirements.need: 10+ years in sales operations or commercial excellence; distributor-based or multi-channel sales
requirements.evidence: Six years across marketing, CRM analytics, and sales operations, including running a 20-person sales team. I support flyExclusive's charter-broker sales channel, and at TRANZACT I delivered analytics and reports to the insurance carriers we partnered with. Industrial distributors would be new; I'd learn TE's channel data (POS, inventory, special pricing) first.

featured.title: From Attribution to Ad Spend
featured.blurb: How I turn conflicting numbers into one decision: count each sale once, compare models side by side, test them, and move budget in capped steps. Includes an interactive scenario model.

featured.title: UTM Journey Tracker — live
featured.blurb: Governance written as code: a controlled list of allowed values, every record checked against it, and failures counted by rule. The same approach I'd use for pricing and commercial data standards.

featured.title: Resume Chat — grounded AI answers
featured.blurb: Answers come from one source of truth and are checked by an automated eval. It's the pattern behind giving sales teams self-serve answers on pricing and policy.
